title: Protocol for derivation of organoids and patient-derived orthotopic xenografts from glioma patient tumors
protocol: Transfer tumor tissue to a glass petri dish under BSC II sterile conditions.
Remove excess medium.
Add 0.5 - 1 mL of fresh organoid medium to ensure sufficient moisture of the tissue during processing.
Mince tumor tissue for approximately 10 - 20 minutes at 20°C–22°C with sterile scalpels until obtaining small tumor fragments invisible by eye (approximately 0.5 mm × 0.5 mm).
Add more medium if needed.
Rinse the petri dish with organoid medium to collect all fragments.
Transfer tissue fragments into a 50 mL falcon tube.
Allow tissue fragments to sediment at 20°C–22°C for approximately 5 min.
Aspirate the medium and resuspend tissue fragments in fresh organoid medium.
Transfer cultures to agar flasks, adjusting volume to reach high culture density.
Incubate the culture flasks in a standard cell culture incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2 and 21% O2.
Verify cultures under the microscope for contamination and tissue fragment size after 1-2 days.
Proceed with medium change after 1 day if pH change is observed.
Monitor organoid cultures on a regular basis.
Change the medium after 5 to 7 days of culture if necessary.
Collect tissue fragments and organoids gently in a 50 mL falcon tube.
Allow organoids to sediment for approximately 5 minutes.
Aspirate the medium.
Resuspend organoids in an appropriate volume of pre-warmed organoid medium.
Transfer cultures to fresh agar flasks.
Culture for 10–14 days before freezing if well-structured organoids are formed or if they start to fuse.
Re-mince fused organoids with scalpels prior to cryopreservation if necessary.
Gently collect the organoids in a 50 mL falcon tube.
Sediment organoids at the bottom of the falcon tube for approximately 5 min.
Aspirate the medium and resuspend organoids in an appropriate volume of ice-cold freezing medium.
Transfer 1 mL of organoids into cryogenic vials.
Place cryogenic vials in a Mr. Frosty freezing container and transfer to -80°C for 12 - 24 h.
After 12–24 h, transfer cryogenic vials to a liquid nitrogen tank for long-term storage.
Thaw cryogenic vials with organoids rapidly at 37°C.
Gently transfer the defrosted solution with organoids to a 15 mL tube.
Add slowly drops of pre-warmed organoid medium up to 3 mL (1 mL per minute).
Shake gently up and down and incubate for 5 min.
Add organoid medium up to 10 mL.
Sediment organoids for approximately 5 minutes.
Aspirate the medium containing DMSO.
Resuspend organoids in fresh organoid medium.
Transfer resuspended organoids to an agar flask.
Culture organoids at 37°C in the incubator for 24 to 72 hours before surgery or experiment.
Collect viable organoids of 400 - 1000 μm under binocular microscope or equivalent.
Gently transfer selected organoids to a 50 mL falcon tube using 2 mL to 10 mL pipette.
Sediment organoids at the bottom of the falcon tube for approximately 5 min.
Aspirate the medium and wash organoids in 10 mL of DMEM w/o supplements.
Repeat washing step 2 times.
Resuspend organoids in 15 mL of DMEM and incubate on ice until surgery.
Inject buprenorphine subcutaneously (volume of injection 10 mL/kg, dose 0.1 mg/kg) to NSG mice to ensure analgesia for 4 - 6 h time period.
Pre-warm the recovery chamber and the cover to 37°C.
Prepare the sterile field with all surgical instruments and reagents needed.
Anesthetize the mouse with an intra-peritoneal injection of a mixture of Ketamine (100 mg/kg) and Xylazine (10 mg/kg).
If available, use gaseous anesthesia by isoflurane to decrease the probability of mouse death due to adverse respiratory effects.
Shave and disinfect the skin using a sterile surgical pad and 70% ethanol.
Protect eyes of the mouse with a drop of Ocry-gel.
Place the head in a stereotaxic frame.
Inject subcutaneously a local anesthetic (Bupivacaine, volume 2 mL/kg; dose 5 mg/kg) on top of the skull.
Disinfect the Hamilton syringe with several flushing of Ethanol followed by 0.9% NaCl.
Transfer organoids to the petri dish and manually aspirate 6 organoids in a maximum volume of 2 μl.
Fix the syringe in the syringe holder of the stereotactic frame.
Perform a short incision (~ 0.7 cm) and open the skin to expose the bregma, sagittal, and coronal sutures.
Place the needle at an angle of 90° to the skull on the bregma to set the 0 position for the X and Y axis on the frame’s ruler.
Place the needle on the surface of the brain to set the 0 position for the Z axis.
Move the needle to the X (2 mm right) and Y (1 mm front) coordinates to locate the drill site.
Drill a small hole with a diameter of 0.7 mm.
Remove remaining bone using the micro-scalpel.
Perform cross incision on the dura mater.
Place the needle on the surface of the brain to set the Z axis position.
Lower the needle 0.5 mm deeper than the specified Z depth (2 mm).
Wait for 2 minutes.
Retract the needle slightly by 0.5 mm.
Inject the organoids slowly at a rate of 1 μl per minute.
Keep the needle in place for 2 more minutes after injection.
Withdraw the needle slowly.
Wash the skull with 0.9% NaCl solution.
Verify if all organoids were implanted correctly.
Close the hole using bone wax.
Close the skin with separate knots (Ethilon 3-0).
Place the animal in a recovery chamber until it recovers from anesthesia.
Monitor the scar carefully for at least 5 to 7 days until knots are no longer visible.
Anesthetize the mouse with 2.5% isoflurane / oxygen mix in the induction chamber.
Transfer the anesthetized mouse to a pre-warmed Minerve bed adapted for mouse head imaging.
Place the motion sensor pillow under the abdomen of the mouse on the Minerve bed.
Maintain body temperature at 37°C and monitor breathing using the motion sensor pillow.
Insert the Minerve bed in the mouse head coil.
Insert the imaging cell containing the animal bed and coil into the magnet tunnel.
Position the mouse's head to reach the isocenter of the magnet.
Check the breathing rate before starting MRI acquisition (PC-SAM software).
Adjust anesthesia mix during the scan session to maintain breathing between 50 and 100 per minute.
Acquire a multislices brain scout using Preclinical software MR solutions.
Verify that the head of the animal is correctly positioned in the isocenter using 3 different plans (sagittal, coronal and transverse).
Position slices packages for the next imaging protocols.
Perform tuning and matching of the coil.
Adjust magnetic field shimming to ensure high quality of the scans.
Select the Axial Fast Spin Echo T2-weighted MRI sequence (FSE T2w Scan).
Properly position the slices packages using anatomical landmarks.
Align the top of the frame with the top of the brain in the coronal plane.
Rotate the frame to correct for animal head side tilting by aligning symmetrical landmarks parallel to the slices in the axial plane.
Align the left side of the frame with the olfactory bulb and cerebellum in the sagittal plane.
Place the first 3 slices to cover the olfactory bulbs.
Start the acquisition of the FSE T2w scan.
Copy the slice position from the previous FSE T2w scan for the Axial Fast Spin Echo T1-weighted MRI sequence (FSE T1w scan).
Paste the slices position and start the acquisition.
Take out the imaging cell from the MRI after the first acquisition.
Avoid displacing the bed or coil to keep the animal in exactly the same position.
Inject subcutaneously 100 μl of Dotarem (Gadoterate 0.5 mmol/mL).
Put back the imaging cell in the machine and wait for 5 minutes.
Start the acquisition of the FSE T1w scan.
Remove the imaging cell from the machine after the acquisition.
Remove the mouse from the bed and place it directly in the cage.
Supervise the mouse until it awakens.
Adjust the brightness of the images.
Delineate the tumor to define the area on each slice.
Sum the tumor areas for tumor volume in mm³ (slice thickness is 1 mm).
Verify the mouse every day.
Fill in the score sheet with observations about common behavior and specific symptoms linked to brain tumors.

Score mice based on symptom severity and body weight loss: 0 = no symptoms, normal behavior; 1 = starting symptoms, ≤5% body weight loss; 2 = established symptoms, >5% to <15% body weight loss; 3 = severe symptoms, ≥15% body weight loss or tumor size ≥100 mm³.
Perform euthanasia if criteria are met: score 2 with one criterion of 3 or score 3.
Euthanize the mouse by cervical dislocation when three symptoms reach a score of 2 or one symptom reaches a score of 3.
Gently extract the brain.
Remove the midbrain.
Mechanically mince brain hemispheres with scalpels.
Select only part of the hemisphere(s) where tumor cells are expected for well-established PDOX models with known histopathological phenotype.
Mechanically dissociate PDOX tumor tissue for single-cell isolation.
Purify human tumor cells from the dissociated brain tissue.
Isolate xenograft-based murine cells constituting the tumor microenvironment (TME).
Apply isolated cells for functional assays.
Reconstitute standardized organoids using purified cells.
Preheat a water bath to 37°C.
Prepare enzyme mix 1 (EM1) by adding components specified in the Neural Tissue Dissociation Kit product leaflet and pre-warm to 37°C to ensure optimal enzymatic activity.
Remove olfactory bulbs (myelin-rich) and midbrain.
Collect part of the brain hemisphere(s) containing tumor cells.
Moist tissue with ice-cold HBSS without Ca2+/Mg2+.
Cut tumor tissue with scalpels for several minutes and transfer the fragments into a 50 mL falcon tube.
Add ice-cold HBSS to the tube up to 20 mL.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 3 minutes at 4°C and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the tissue pellet in EM1.
Incubate the resuspended tissue in a water bath at 37°C for 15 minutes, mixing gently every 5 minutes.
Prepare enzyme mix 2 (EM2) as specified in the product leaflet.
Add EM2 to the tissue and incubate for 10 minutes at 37°C, mixing gently every 5 minutes during this period.
Repeat mechanical dissociation with a glass pipette by pipetting up and down ten times, avoiding air bubbles.
If necessary, incubate another 10 minutes at 37°C if tissue fragments are visible.
Add 10 mL HBSS to the dissociated tissue.
Filter cells through a 50 μm sterile filter into a 15 mL falcon tube.
Centrifuge the single cell suspension at 300 g for 3 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend tissue pellet in 1800 μl ice-cold MACS buffer per PDOX tumor.
Add 200 μl of Myelin Removal Beads II to the resuspended tissue.
Mix gently, do not vortex.
Incubate for 15 min in the refrigerator at 4°C.
Wash cells by adding 13 mL ice-cold MACS buffer and centrifuge at 300 g for 10 min.
Aspirate supernatant completely.
Add 3 mL of MACS buffer per 200 μl of Myelin Removal Beads II.
Use 3 LS columns per PDOX tumor.
Place 50 μm sterile filter on top of each column.
Rinse each LS column with 3 × 1 ml ice-cold MACS buffer and discard collected buffer.
Transfer 1 mL of single cell suspension through each filter and LS column.
Collect flow-through fraction containing single cells.
Wash columns with 3 × 1 mL of ice-cold MACS buffer, collect in the same falcon tubes.
Pool collected cells from 3 falcon tubes.
Adjust volume to 20 mL with ice-cold MACS buffer.
Count the cells.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate buffer and resuspend cell pellet: 80 μl ice-cold MACS buffer per 2 × 10⁶ tumor cells or 10⁷ total cells including red blood cells.
Add 20 μl cell depletion cocktail per cell suspension in 80 μl ice-cold MACS buffer.
Incubate for 15 min at 4°C in the fridge (do not incubate on ice).
Adjust volume to 500 μl using ice-cold MACS buffer for up to 2 × 10⁶ tumor cells or up to 10⁷ total cells.
Place one LS column per cell suspension in 80 μl ice-cold MACS buffer on top of a magnetic field of a suitable MACS® magnetic cell separator.
Rinse each LS column with 3 × 1 ml MACS buffer and collect the buffer in 15 ml falcon tubes.
Place new 15 ml collection flacon tubes under the columns on ice.
Apply cell suspension to the LS column(s).
Collect flow through fraction containing human tumor cells.
Wash LS column(s) with 5 × 1 ml of ice-cold MACS buffer and collect flow through fraction.
Wash the column with 3 mL ice-cold MACS buffer if desired for mouse cell collection.
Push buffer through the column with the plunger after removing it from the magnetic cell separator.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 300 g for 3 min at 4°C.
Resuspend cell pellet in an appropriate buffer or medium for downstream applications.
Incubate tumor cells in 50 mL falcon tube in organoid medium for 20–30 min after defrosting.
Count cells to determine number of viable cells using dead cell staining.
Seed 1000 cells per well in 25 μl organoid medium in a 384-well u-shaped, low adherence plate.
Adapt volume to 50 μl for 96-well plates if necessary.
Fill unused wells with 90 μl HBSS according to the plate layout.
Avoid seeding of cells in outer wells and edge well regions due to potential edge effect phenomenon on organoids during longer experimental protocols.
Centrifuge 384-well plates to pellet cells softly at maximum 300 g for 3–5 min at 4°C.
If cells do not assemble at the bottom of the plate, repeat centrifugation.
Place plates on a 3D shaker in a standard incubator and shake at high speed (approximately 30 – 40 rpm) for 48 h to allow for organoid formation.
Proceed to the experimental protocol.
Add 25 μl of organoid medium containing desired compound(s) to reach total volume of 50 μl.
